rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited Arabic line uses nasiya for someone forgotten or disregarded, illustrating Mary’s wish to be forgotten.
rows.anchor: أتجعلنا جسرا لكلب قضاعة … ولست بنسي في معد ولا دخل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha wished that, when she died, she would be forgotten and unremembered.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أنها قالت: لوددت أني إذا مت كنت نسيا منسيا

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce min taḥtihā with kasra and identify the caller as Gabriel calling from the mountain slope.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي: من تحتها بكسر الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers pronounce min taḥtihā with fatḥa and identify the caller as Jesus emerging from Mary’s womb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون من تحتها بفتح الميم وهو عيسى لما خرج من بطنها ناداها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the sariy as Jesus, a noble and elevated servant.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: يعني عيسى كان والله عبدا سريا أي رفيعا

rows.speaker: سائر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators interpret the sariy as a small river.
rows.anchor:
وقال سائر المفسرين:
هو النهر الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Beneath you” can mean that the river was placed under Mary’s command, flowing or stopping at her direction.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى جعل النهر تحت أمرها إن أمرته أن يجري جرى وإن أمرته بالإمساك أمسك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Gabriel—or, in another version, Jesus—struck the ground; a fresh spring appeared, and the dried palm revived, blossomed, fruited, and ripened.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فضرب جبرئيل: ويقال عيسى: برجله الأرض فظهرت عين ماء عذب وجرى وحييت النخلة بعد يبسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huzzi means move or shake toward yourself; Arabic allows the preposition to accompany verbs that also take a direct object.
rows.anchor: وقيل لمريم وهزي إليك أي حركي بجذع النخلة يقول العرب: هزه وهز به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jidhʿ can mean either a branch or the palm tree itself.
rows.anchor: والجذع: الغصن، والجذع: النخلة نفسها

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وحماد ونصير
rows.claim: These readers have the masculine-form reading yusāqiṭ, referring back to the palm trunk.
rows.anchor: قرأ البراء بن عازب ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وحماد ونصير: يساقط بالياء

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads tusāqiṭ with a light sin and kasra on the qaf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص تساقط بضم التاء وتخفيف السين وكسر القاف

rows.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة وأبو عبيد
rows.claim: These readers use the feminine reading with a doubled sin, referring to the palm tree.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة وأبو عبيد: تساقط بفتح التاء والقاف وتشديد السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine reading refers to the palm, the masculine to the trunk; doubling uses assimilation, while the light reading uses deletion.
rows.anchor:
فمن أنث رده إلى النخلة ومن ذكر رده ألى الجذع والتشديد على الإدغام
والتخفيف على الحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rutab janiyy means a fresh, moist fruit at the moment of picking.
rows.anchor: رطبا جنيا غصنا رطبا ساعة جني

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says dates are the best food for a woman after childbirth and honey for a sick person.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن خيثم: ما للنفساء عندي خير من الرطب ولا للمريض من العسل

rows.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maymun says dates are best for a woman whose labor is difficult, citing the palm-tree verse.
rows.anchor: وقال عمرو بن ميمون: ما أدري للمرأة إذا عسر عليها ولدها خير من الرطب لقول الله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha calls date-palm rubbing on a newborn’s palate a Prophetic practice; the Prophet chewed dates and applied them to Companions’ children.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: إن من السنة أن يمضغ التمر ويدلك به فم المولود

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأنس
rows.claim: Their reading glosses ṣawman as ṣamtan, meaning silence.
rows.anchor: أي صمتا ولذلك كان بقراءة ابن مسعود وأنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary Arabic, ṣawm is restraint from food and speech.
rows.anchor: والصوم في اللغة هو الإمساك عن الطعام والكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse abbreviates the instruction: if asked about the child or blamed, Mary should say she vowed silence to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية اختصار فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فسألك عن ولدك أو لامك عليه فقولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God told Mary to answer by gesture; another says she was to say the words aloud and then stop speaking.
rows.anchor: يقال: إن الله أمرها أن تقول هذا اشارة ويقال: أمرها أن تقوله نطقا ثم تمسك عن الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that Mary spoke to angels but did not speak to human beings.
rows.anchor: يقال: كانت تكلم الملائكة ولا تكلم الإنس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Joseph the carpenter took Mary and Jesus to a cave for forty days until she recovered from childbirth, then brought her back.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: احتمل يوسف النجار مريم وابنها عيسى (عليه السلام) إلى غار

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: On the way back Jesus reassured Mary that he was God’s servant and Messiah; her pious family wept when she arrived carrying him.
rows.anchor: فكلمها عيسى في الطريق فقال: يا أماه أبشري فإني عبد الله ومسيحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fariyy means something shocking, reprehensible, or immense; Abu ʿUbayda says it applies to anything astonishing or to an act.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: كل من عجب أو عمل فهو فري

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said he had never seen a genius match ʿUmar’s remarkable performance.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في عمر رضي الله عنه: «فلم أر عبقريا يفري فريه

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz poet uses fariyy for saying much and magnifying a matter.
rows.anchor:
قال الراجز:
قد أطعمتني دقلا حوليا … مسوسا مدودا حجريا
قد كنت تفرين به الفريا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet explains “sister of Aaron” as referring to a woman of Aaron’s prophetic lineage.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «انما عنوا هارون النبي أخا موسى

rows.speaker: قتادة وغيره
rows.claim: Qatada and others identify Aaron as a pious Israelite, not Moses’ brother; forty thousand Israelites named Aaron followed his funeral.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وغيره: كان هارون رجلا صالحا من أتقياء بني إسرائيل وليس بهارون أخي موسى

rows.speaker: المغيرة بن شعبة
rows.claim: People of Najran raised the chronological gap between Moses and Jesus; the Prophet replied that people named themselves after earlier prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: وقال المغيرة بن شعبة: قال لي أهل نجران قوله: يا أخت هارون وقد كان بين موسى وعيسى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Aaron was Mary’s paternal half-brother and an exemplary Israelite.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كان هارون أخا مريم من أبيها ليس من أمها وكان أمثل رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Aaron was Israel’s most corrupt man and Mary was likened to him; here “sister” means likeness, as Arabic calls a likeness a sibling.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن هارون كان من أفسق بني إسرائيل وأظهرهم فسادا فشبهوها به، وعلى هذا القول الأخت هاهنا بمعنى الشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke invokes Mary’s father ʿImran as no evil man and her mother Hannah as no prostitute, asking where this child came from.
rows.anchor: ما كان أبوك عمران امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك حنة بغيا زانية فمن أين لك هذا الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary gestures toward Jesus, directing the people to speak to him.
rows.anchor: فأشارت مريم إلى عيسى أن كلموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the cradle” is explained as the place where Jesus lay, namely Mary’s lap; another view takes it as a literal cradle.
rows.anchor: من هو في المهد وهو حجرها، وقيل: هو المهد بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A grammatical view treats kāna as redundant in the construction, like “you were the best community” or “was I anything but a human messenger?”
rows.anchor: وقد كان حشوا للكلام ولا معنى له كقوله كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line is cited as poetic evidence for the construction in which kāna is redundant.
rows.anchor:
قال زهير:
أجرت عليه حرة أرحبية … وقد كان لون الليل مثل الأرندج

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line likewise omits a meaning-bearing role for kāna in “neighbors who were noble.”
rows.anchor:
وقال الفرزدق:
فكيف إذا رأيت ديار قومي … وجيران لنا كانوا كرام

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Zakariya, while disputing with the Jews, asked Jesus to state his proof; Jesus spoke at forty days old.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: فأتاها زكريا عند مناظرتها اليهود فقال لعيسى: انطق بحجتك إن كنت أمرت بها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Jesus spoke on the day he was born.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هو يوم ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ first words affirm servitude to God, refuting the Christians and establishing the proof against them.
rows.anchor: فأقر على نفسه بالعبودية لله تعالى أول ما تكلم تكذيبا للنصارى وإلزاما للحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maymun says the people took stones to throw at Mary, but left her when Jesus spoke; Jesus then remained silent until ordinary childhood.
rows.anchor: إن مريم لما أتت قومها بعيسى أخذوا لها الحجارة ليرموها فلما تكلم عيسى تركوها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report lists five who spoke before the usual age: Joseph’s witness, Pharaoh’s hairdresser’s child, Jesus, Jurayj’s companion, and the child of the trench-burned woman.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: خمسة تكلموا قبل إبان الكلام: شاهد يوسف، وولد ماشطة بنت فرعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: During the Night Journey the Prophet smelled a pleasant fragrance; Gabriel said it came from Pharaoh’s hairdresser, who declared God her Lord and endured the killing of her children, including an infant who urged her to persevere in truth.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أسري به مرت به رائحة طيبة فقال: يا جبرئيل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report recounts Jurayj choosing prayer over his mother on three visits; she prayed he would see the city’s prostitutes, and the Prophet noted that a prayer for his temptation would have been answered.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurayj was falsely accused after a shepherd impregnated a village woman; he asked the infant who his father was, and the child named the shepherd, clearing him. Jurayj asked people to restore his cell as before.
rows.anchor: وكان راعي ضأن يأوي إلى ديره، فخرجت امرأة من القرية فوقع عليها فحملت فولدت غلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says he will recount the child of the trench later.
rows.anchor: وأما ولد صاحبة الأخدود فسنذكرها في موضعها إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He gave me the Book” has past form but future meaning; another view says it refers to what was written for Jesus in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: آتاني الكتاب يعني يؤتيني الكتاب لفظه ماض ومعناه مستقبل، وقيل: إنه أخبر عما كتب له في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asked when he was appointed a prophet, the Prophet said he was written as a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body.
rows.anchor: سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: متى كتبت نبيا؟ قال: «كتبت نبيا وآدم بين الروح والجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God taught and inspired Jesus with the Torah while he was in his mother’s womb.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه علمني وألهمني التوراة في بطن أمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was made a teacher of good wherever he went; another explanation says he was a blessing to those who followed his religion and command.
rows.anchor: معلما للخير أين ما كنت وقيل: مباركا على من اتبع ديني وأمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enjoined prayer and almsgiving for Jesus’ lifetime, made him dutiful to his mother, and not tyrannical or wretched.
rows.anchor: وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا وبرا أي وجعلني برا بوالدتي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A woman praised Jesus’ pregnancy and nursing; he replied that blessed is whoever recites and follows God’s Book, and described himself as humble, soft-hearted, and small in his own estimation.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا ان امرأة رأت عيسى ابن مريم يحيي الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ greeting of peace covers his birth, death, and being raised alive.
rows.anchor: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing identifies Jesus himself as “the word of truth”; another treats the phrase as repetition, “that is Jesus son of Mary, and that is the word of truth.”
rows.anchor: ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق يعني هو قول الحق، وقيل: رفع على التكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing makes “word of truth” an adjective for Jesus, meaning God’s word, with al-Ḥaqq referring to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو نعت لعيسى يعني ذلك عيسى بن مريم كلمة الله، والحق هو الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers put qawl in the accusative, meaning that Jesus said the word of truth about which people dispute.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر ويعقوب قول بالنصب يعني قال قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People dispute Jesus’ identity: Jews call him a lying magician, while Christians call him God’s son and one of three.
rows.anchor: فقالت اليهود: ساحر كذاب، وقالت النصارى: ابن الله وثالث ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s taking a child is incompatible with His nature; alternatively the lām is transposed, meaning God would never take a child; creation occurs by His command.
rows.anchor: ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد أي ما كان من صفته اتخاذ الولد، وقيل: اللام منقولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And that God is my Lord” means that He decreed it; the Kufan readers begin with inna under kasra as a fresh sentence.
rows.anchor:
وإن الله يعني وقضى أن الله، وقرأ أهل الكوفة إن الله
بالكسر على الاستيناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshiping God is the straight path just described.
rows.anchor: ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا الذي ذكرت صراط مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The factions are Christian groups divided over Jesus into Nestorians, Melkites, and Jacobites.
rows.anchor: سموا أحزابا لأنهم تجزأوا ثلاث فرق في أمر عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How well they hear and see” is an expression of amazement: at Resurrection they hear and see when neither faculty can benefit them.
rows.anchor: أسمع بهم وأبصر يعني ما أسمعهم وأبصرهم، على التعجب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says no one will hear or see more keenly on Resurrection Day, when God asks Jesus whether he told people to worship him.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: لا أحد يوم القيامة أسمع منهم ولا أبصر حين يقول الله سبحانه وتعالى لعيسى أنت قلت للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Regret is when judgment is finished, the people of Paradise and Hell have entered their abodes, and death is slaughtered; people in worldly life remain heedless.
rows.anchor: إذ قضي الأمر أي فرغ من الحساب وأدخل أهل الجنة الجنة وأهل النار النار وذبح الموت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet describes death as a black-and-white ram, slaughtered after the inhabitants of Paradise and Hell are asked to recognize it; each side is then told its fate is everlasting, intensifying joy and grief.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يجاء بالموت يوم القيامة كأنه كبش أملح

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says that without God’s decree of the Fire’s residents’ eternal life, they would die of grief when they saw their fate.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: لولا ما قضى الله سبحانه وتعالى من تخليد أهل النار وتعميرهم فيها لماتوا حسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits the earth by causing everyone on it to die while He remains.
rows.anchor: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها أي نميتهم ويبقى الرب عز وجل فيرثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone returns to God so He can repay them for their deeds.
rows.anchor: وإلينا يرجعون فنجزيهم بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is described as a truthful, believing, certain, prophetic messenger of high rank; he addresses his father Azar, whose idols neither hear nor see nor help.
rows.anchor:
واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا مؤمنا موقنا صدوقا نبيا رسولا رفيعا إذ قال لأبيه
آزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s God-given knowledge and clear proof concern the afterlife and punishment of those who worship other than God; following Abraham leads to an upright path.
rows.anchor: إني قد جاءني من العلم والبيان بعد الموت وأن من غيره عذبه ما لم يأتك فاتبعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshiping Satan means obeying him; whoever obeys something has worshiped it. Kāna can mean “is” or “became.”
rows.anchor: لا تطعه، لم تصل، له ولم تصم وإن من أطاع شيئا فقد عبده إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “I fear” is explained as “I know”; related constructions use the same verb for fearing spouses will fail to uphold God’s limits.
rows.anchor: إني أخاف أعلم أن يمسك يصيبك عذاب من الرحمن لقوله: إلا أن يخافا وقوله فإن خفتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Abraham feared a worldly punishment would fall on his father, leaving him Satan’s companion in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إني أخاف أن ينزل عليك عذابا في الدنيا فتكون للشيطان وليا قرينا في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father’s question means: Are you turning away from and abandoning worship of my idols?
rows.anchor: أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم تارك عبادتهم وزاهد فيهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi interpret the threat to stone Abraham as a threat to insult him.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي: لأشتمنك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the threat as beating Abraham.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لأضربنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the father threatened to expose Abraham’s situation.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأظهرن أمرك

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعطاء
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and ʿAta say “leave me for a long while” means leave me safe and unharmed.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وعطاء: سالما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as leaving him without blame or reproach.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: واعتزلني سالم العرض لا يصيبنك مني معرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the phrase to mean abandoning him for a long time and not speaking to him.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: اتركني واجتنبني طويلا فلا تكلمني

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains maliyy as a period of time.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: دهرا

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Mujahid and ʿIkrima explain it as “for a while”; the root connotes staying a long time, and al-malawan are night and day.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة: حينا، وأصل الحرف المكث، ومنه يقال: تمليت حينا، والملوان الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s greeting means that his father is safe from harm at Abraham’s hands.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم سلام عليك أي سلمت مني لا أصيبك بمكروه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil explain ḥafiyyan as gentle and merciful.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: لطيفا رحيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss for ḥafiyyan is kind and devoted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بارا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means God has made a habit of answering Abraham.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عوده الإجابة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Abraham knew God would answer when called upon.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عالما يستجيب لي إذا دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s resolve is to leave his people and the idols they worship.
rows.anchor: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله يعني وأعتزل ما تعبدون من دون الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Abraham left his people at Kutha and migrated to the Holy Land.
rows.anchor:
قال مقاتل:
كان اعتزاله إياهم أنه فارقهم من كوثى فهاجر منها إلى الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham hopes his prayer will be answered and he will not be disappointed; alternatively, he hopes not to suffer through worship as idolaters do.
rows.anchor:
عسى أن يجيبني ولا يخيبني، وقيل:
معناه عسى أن لا أشقى بدعائه وعبادته كما تشقون أنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham left his people and their idols to migrate, God granted him Isaac and Jacob, and made Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob prophets.
rows.anchor: فذهب مهاجرا وهبنا له بعد الهجرة إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy here means His gifts; al-Kalbi specifies wealth and children, while another view specifies prophecy and scripture.
rows.anchor: ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا نعمتنا، قال الكلبي: المال والولد، وقيل: النبوة والكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “lofty truthful renown” is excellent, elevated praise among all religions, whose adherents honor them.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا يعني ثناء حسنا رفيعا في كل أهل الأديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sincere and free of hypocrisy; Muqatil glosses this as Muslim and affirming God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا يعني غير مرائي، قال مقاتل : مسلما موحدا

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufan readers use the passive-like form mukhlaṣan, meaning God purified and chose Moses.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة: مخلصا بفتح اللام يعني أخلصناه واخترناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God called and spoke to Moses on Friday night from the right side of the mountain, which lies between Egypt and Midian.
rows.anchor: وناديناه دعوناه وكلمناه ليلة الجمعة من جانب الطور الأيمن يعني يمين موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Moses was raised through the heavens and veils until only one veil remained between him and God.
rows.anchor: وقربناه نجيا يعني رفعناه من سماء إلى سماء ومن حجاب إلى حجاب حتى لم يكن بينه وبينه إلا حجاب واحد

rows.speaker: ميسرة
rows.claim: Maysara says God brought Moses so close that he heard the scratching of the pen.
rows.anchor: عن ميسرة وقربناه نجيا قال: قربه حتى سمع صريف القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najiyy means one engaged in private conversation, like a close companion or table companion.
rows.anchor: والنجي: المناجي كالجليس والنديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses Aaron as a prophet in response to Moses’ request for Aaron as a minister and messenger.
rows.anchor: ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا وذلك حين سأل موسى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is Ishmael son of Abraham; he fulfilled his promises.
rows.anchor: واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل يعني ابن إبراهيم إنه كان صادق الوعد كان إذا وعد أنجز

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Ishmael promised a man to wait and stayed at the meeting place three days until the man returned.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه وعد رجلا أن يقيم مكانه حتى يرجع إليه فأقام إسماعيل مكانه ثلاثة أيام للميعاد حتى يرجع إليه الرجل، قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Ishmael waited for the promised man until a full year had passed.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: انتظره حتى حال الحول عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was a messenger and prophet who conveyed God’s message to his people.
rows.anchor: وكان رسولا إلى قومه نبيا مخبرا عن الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael commanded his family—meaning his people—to pray and give alms, and was righteous and pure in God’s sight.
rows.anchor: وكان يأمر أهله يعني قومه وكذلك هو في حرف ابن مسعود بالصلاة والزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris was Noah’s great-grandfather, called Akhnukh; his name reflects extensive study of books, and he was a tailor, first to write with a pen and sew and wear sewn clothes, and first to study astronomy and calculation.
rows.anchor: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس وهو جد أبي نوح، فسمي إدريس لكثرة درسه الكتب، واسمه أخنوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “high place” to which Idris was raised means Paradise.
rows.anchor: ورفعناه مكانا عليا يعني الجنة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Idris was raised to the sixth heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: رفع إلى السماء السادسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places Idris in the fourth heaven.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الرابعة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada transmits Anas ibn Malik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa’s report that the Prophet saw Idris in the fourth heaven during the Ascension.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ورفعناه مكانا عليا قال: حدثنا أنس بن مالك بن صعصعة أن النبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب وغيرهما
rows.claim: A report says Idris prayed that God lighten the sun-bearing angel’s load and heat; God answered his prayer, after which the angel asked to meet him.
rows.anchor: على ما قاله ابن عباس وكعب وغيرهما أنه سار ذات يوم في حاجة فأصابه وهج الشمس فقال: يا رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one narrative the sun-bearing angel asks the Angel of Death to delay Idris’ term; Death instead reveals that Idris’ appointed death is at sunrise, where the angel had left him, and Idris is found dead.
rows.anchor: فكان مما سأله أن قال له: أخبرت أنك أكرم الملائكة وأمكنهم عند ملك الموت فاشفع لي إليه

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb gives another account: angels marvel at Idris’ worship, and the Angel of Death visits him; Idris asks for his soul to be taken and restored so he can experience death and prepare for it.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: كان يرفع لإدريس كل يوم من العبادة مثل ما يرفع لجميع أهل الأرض في زمانه

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: In Wahb’s account Idris also asks to see heaven, Paradise, and Hell; after entering Paradise he clings to a tree and refuses to leave.
rows.anchor: ثم قال إدريس له: لي إليك حاجة أخرى، قال: وما هي؟ قال: ترفعني إلى السماء لأنظر إليها وإلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris refuses to leave Paradise, citing that he has tasted death, passed through Hell, and that its inhabitants are never expelled; God confirms that he remains there by divine command.
rows.anchor: كل نفس ذائقة الموت وقد ذقته، وقال وإن منكم إلا واردها وقد وردتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This story explains the statement that Idris was raised to a high place.
rows.anchor: فهو حي هناك فذلك قوله: ورفعناه مكانا عليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed people include prophets from Adam’s descendants, those carried with Noah, descendants of Abraham and Israel, and people God guided to Islam and chose above others.
rows.anchor: وممن هدينا إلى الإسلام واجتبينا على الأنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukiy is a plural meaning “weeping,” formed like other plurals of participles.
rows.anchor: خروا سجدا وبكيا جمع باك تقديره من الفعل فعول مثل ساجد وسجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed about the believing People of the Book, including ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions.
rows.anchor: نزلت في مؤمني أهل الكتاب، عبد الله سلام وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successors who came after the prophets were wicked people; the verse refers to the Jews and those who followed them.
rows.anchor: فخلف من بعدهم يعيني من بعد النبيين المذكورين خلف وهم قوم سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexical distinction says khalaf with fatḥ is righteous, khalaf with ḍamm is wicked, and sukūn marks what is defective generally.
rows.anchor: والخلف بالفتح الصالح، والخلف بالحزم الطالح، والخلف بسكون اللام الرديء من كل شيء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say the successors are from this Muslim community.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: في هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting prayer means abandoning the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: أضاعوا الصلاة أي تركوا الصلوات المفروضة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وإبراهيم والقاسم بن مخيمرة
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibrahim, and al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymira say they delayed prayers beyond their appointed times.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود وإبراهيم والقاسم بن مخيمرة: أخروها عن مواقيتها وصلوها بغير وقتها

rows.speaker: قرة بن خالد
rows.claim: Qurra ibn Khalid recounts that al-Dahhak delayed the afternoon prayer until sunset neared and said he would rather be called to account than neglect it.
rows.anchor: قال قرة بن خالد: استبطأ الضحاك مرة امتراء في صلاة العصر حتى كادت الشمس تغرب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads “the prayers” in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: أضاعوا الصلوات

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets following desires as permitting marriage to one’s paternal half-sister.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: استحلوا نكاح الأخت من الأب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets desires as pleasures such as drinking wine and other indulgences.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني اللذات وشرب الخمر وغيره

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid places this corruption near the Hour, after the righteous of Muhammad’s community are gone, when people fornicate in streets and alleys.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: هذا عند اقتراب الساعة وذهاب صالحي أمة محمد

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the Prophet connected the verse to a generation appearing sixty years later that would neglect prayer and follow desires.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الآية قال: يكون خلف من بعد ستين سنة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAli says this applies when monumental buildings are built, conspicuous mounts are ridden, and famous clothing is worn.
rows.anchor: وقال على بن أبي طالب: «هذا إذا بني المشيد وركب المنظور ولبس المشهور

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb portrays the successors as drinkers, gamblers, followers of lusts, and neglecters of Friday congregations and prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: فخلف من بعدهم خلف شرابون للقهوات، لعابون بالكعبات، ركابون للشهوات

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says that at the end of time men will beat people with whips like cow tails, then cites this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: يظهر في آخر الزمان أقوام بأيديهم سياط كأذناب البقر يضربون الناس

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies ghayy as a fire in Hell.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: الغي نار في جهنم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies ghayy as a valley in Hell whose heat other valleys seek refuge from; it is prepared for persistent adulterers, drunkards, usurers, the undutiful, false witnesses, and women who ascribe another man’s child to their husbands.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الغى واد في جهنم وإن أودية جهنم لتستعيذ من حرها

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta says ghayy is a valley of pus and blood in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: الغى واد في جهنم يسيل قيحا ودما

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb describes ghayy as a deep, foul-tasting river in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: الغى نهر في النار بعيد قعره، خبيث طعمه

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb calls ghayy Hell’s deepest and hottest valley, with a well that rekindles the Fire when it subsides.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: هو واد في جهنم أبعدها قعرا وأشدها حرا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses ghayy as loss; other glosses are punishment, pain, and disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: خسرانا وقيل: عذابا، وقيل: ألما، وقيل: كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent, believe, and act righteously enter Paradise without being wronged.
rows.anchor: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised Gardens of Eden are unseen by the servants, and maʾtiyyan means that the promise will come to pass.
rows.anchor: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب ولم يروها إنه كان وعده مأتيا يعني آتيا

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s line is cited as poetic evidence that maʾtiyyan means coming.
rows.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
وساعيت معصيا إليها وشاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise contains no vain, obscene, or excessive speech; Muqatil specifies false oaths, while greetings of peace are heard from one another and the angels.
rows.anchor: لا يسمعون فيها في الجنة لغوا باطلا وفحشا وفضولا من الكلام، قال مقاتل: يمينا كاذبة إلا سلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening provision indicates an amount corresponding to the two ends of the day.
rows.anchor: ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا يعني على مقدار طرفي النهار

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir says Arabs considered a person who had both lunch and dinner well provided; the verse promises an interval’s provision.
rows.anchor: عن يحيى بن أبي كثير قال: كانت العرب في زمانها من وجد غداء مع عشاء فذلك هو الناعم

rows.speaker: زهير بن محمد
rows.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad says Paradise has no night and remains in light; its residents sense night and day by curtains being lowered and raised.
rows.anchor: قال: سألت زهير بن محمد عن قول الله سبحانه ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا قال: ليس في الجنة ليل

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqub reads nurith with doubled th; the preferred light form accords with another verse about inheritance.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب: نورث بالتشديد، والاختيار التخفيف لقوله ثم أورثنا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا جبرئيل ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Gabriel delayed, then asked why the Muslims did not trim nails, shorten moustaches, or use tooth-sticks; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor:
وقال مجاهد: أبطأت الرسل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أتاه جبرئيل فقال:
ما حبسك

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومقاتل وقتادة والكلبي
rows.claim: They say Gabriel’s visit was delayed while the Prophet awaited answers about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; the delay distressed him and pagans said his Lord had forsaken him.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك ومقاتل وقتادة والكلبي: احتبس جبرئيل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين سأله قومه عن قصة أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says Gabriel’s delay lasted forty days.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the delay lasted twelve nights; another view says fifteen.
rows.anchor:
وقال مجاهد: اثنتي عشرة ليلة وقيل:
خمس عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes these words the speech of Paradise’s inhabitants, saying the gardens descend only by God’s command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا إخبار عن أهل الجنة، أنهم يقولون عند دخولها: ما تتنزل هذه الجنان إلا بأمر الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains what is before the angels as the afterlife, what is behind them as worldly life, and what is between as the period between the two trumpet blasts—forty years.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: له ما بين أيدينا من أمر الآخرة وما خلفنا من أمر الدنيا وما بين ذلك يعني بين النفختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify the domains as creation, the end of lifespans, and lifetime; or the afterlife’s reward and punishment, past deeds, and what remains until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان له ابتداء خلقنا وله كان منتهى آجالنا، وله كان مدة حياتنا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Gabriel that the delay caused him distress and longing; Gabriel replied that he descends only when commanded and remains absent when held back.
rows.anchor: قال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أبطأت علي حتى ساء ظني واشتقت إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further readings of “what is before and behind us” cover afterlife recompense, past worldly deeds, and all that will happen before Resurrection; another view means before creation, after death, and present life.
rows.anchor: ويقال: ما بين أيدينا من الثواب والعقاب وأمور الآخرة وما خلفنا ما مضى من أعمالنا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the angels, the phrase can refer to earth, heaven, and what lies between; all belong to God, so nothing can be done except by His command.
rows.anchor: ويقال له ما بين أيدينا إلى الأرض إذا أردنا النزول إليها وما خلفنا أي السماء إذا نزلنا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not forgetful: when He wills to send a revelation, He sends it.
rows.anchor: وما كان ربك نسيا أي ناسيا إذا شاء أن يرسل إليك أرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands worship and patient perseverance in worship of the Lord of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses samiyyan as an equal or counterpart to God.
rows.anchor:
قال ابن عباس:
مثلا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses samiyyan as a match.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: عدلا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reads the question as asking whether anyone besides God is called Allah.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هل تعلم أحدا يسمى الله غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human in the verse is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, mocking and denying resurrection from the grave.
rows.anchor: ويقول الإنسان يعني أبي بن خلف الجمحي أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج من القبر حيا استهزاء وتكذيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “does the human not remember?” means reflect and think; its underlying form is yatadhakkar.
rows.anchor: أولا يذكر أي يتذكر ويتفكر، والأصل يتذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ونافع وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use the light reading yadhkur; the author prefers the doubled reading because of a related verse, and Ubay’s reading supports it.
rows.anchor:
وقرأ ابن عامر ونافع
وعاصم ويعقوب يذكر بالتخفيف، والاختيار التشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears to gather the deniers of resurrection together with the devils who misled them, chaining each unbeliever to a devil.
rows.anchor: لنحشرنهم لنجمعنهم في المعاد يعني المشركين المنكرين للبعث والشياطين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says jithiyyan means assembled in groups.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: جماعات جماعات

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says jithiyyan means all together and treats it as a plural of a heap.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: جميعا وهو على هذا القول جمع جثوة

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Hasan and al-Dahhak say the people are kneeling on their knees; here jithiyyan is a plural of “kneeling.”
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن والضحاك: جاثية على الركب وهو على هذا التأويل جمع جاث

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt’s verse is cited as poetic evidence for jithiyyan, describing leaders abandoned kneeling and chained.
rows.anchor:
قال الكميت:
هم تركوا سراتهم جثيا … وهم دون السراة مقرنينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shīʿa here is a community or religious group; God will extract the most rebellious among each.
rows.anchor: لنخرجن من كل أمة وأهل دين أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rebellion as audacity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني جرأة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses it as wickedness and lying.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: فجورا وكذبا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses it as arrogance; other views call it excess or disbelief.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: علوا، وقيل: غلوا في الكفر، وقيل: كفرا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the most rebellious person as each group’s evil leader.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قائدهم رأسهم في الشر

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says the judgment begins with the most prominent; the verse means God knows best who most deserves to enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص قال: نبدأ بالأكابر فالأكابر ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣilyan is the verbal noun of entering and burning in the Fire, with alternate forms patterned on common verb nouns.
rows.anchor: أي أحق بدخول النار، يقال: صلي يصلى صليا مثل لقي يلقى لقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There is none of you but will arrive at it” contains an omitted oath and means everyone arrives at Hell.
rows.anchor:
قيل: في الآية إضمار مجازه: والله إن منكم يعني ما منكم من
أحد إلا واردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People disagree about arrival according to their views on the threat: the threat absolutists say none who enters leaves, while the Murjiʾa say no believer enters.
rows.anchor: واختلف الناس في معنى الورود حسب اختلافهم في الوعيد، فأما الوعيد فإنهم قالوا : إن من دخلها لم يخرج منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues from the Pharaoh passage and the passage about idols and their worshipers: unless arrival means entering, they would have to enter Paradise after merely passing Hell.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا، بقول الله سبحانه حكاية عن فرعون يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All sides agree that wurud means presence or passing; Sunni scholars say it means entry, and that God may punish sinful believers and then release them.
rows.anchor: حكاية عن فرعون يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following promise to save the God-fearing proves arrival means entering, since rescue is only from something one has entered; Arabic usage also means entering a place.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل على أن الورود هو الدخول قوله في سياق الآية ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says further proof from Prophetic tradition follows.
rows.anchor: ودليلنا أيضا من السنة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet said every righteous and wicked person enters Hell, which becomes cool and safe for believers as it did for Abraham; then the God-fearing are rescued and wrongdoers left kneeling.
rows.anchor: فلقيت جابر بن عبد الله فسألته فأهوى بإصبعيه إلى أذنيه وقال: صمتا إن لم أكن سمعت النبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas argues with Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq that the passages about idols and Pharaoh mean entering; he says they too will arrive at Hell and hopes God will bring him out, unlike the denier.
rows.anchor: فتلا ابن عباس حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردون أدخل هؤلاء أم لا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says people enter Hell and then emerge from it according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله وإن منكم إلا واردها قال: يردونها ثم يصدرون عنها بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud describes the bridge over Hell as sharp as a sword’s edge; people cross at varying speeds, while angels pray for their safety.
rows.anchor:
عن أبي الأحوص عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال:
الصراط على جهنم مثل حد السيف

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says a Muslim who loses three children will not enter the Fire except as fulfillment of the oath, then recites this verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله عليه السلام: ما من مسلم يموت له ثلاث من الولد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan tells a story of a man asking his brother whether he knows he will enter Hell and whether he knows he will leave; the brother stops laughing when he cannot say he will leave.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رجل لأخيه: أي أخ هل أتاك أنك وارد النار

rows.speaker: ابن ميسرة
rows.claim: Ibn Maysara wishes his mother had not borne him: although guided to Islam, he knows the text says people enter Hell but sees no promise that they emerge; he cites a verse to that effect.
rows.anchor: عن ابن ميسرة أنه أوى إلى فراشه فقال: يا ليت أمي لم تلدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not single out the prophets by asserting that they enter Hell; rather, say that all creatures arrive at it.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: فخبرونا عن الأنبياء هل يدخلون النار؟ يقال لهم: لا تطلق هذه اللفظة بالتخصيص فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ arrival at Midian’s water meant entry: he drew water for Shuʿayb’s daughters, watered the flock, and stayed there; Arabic also names people by their water.
rows.anchor: فإن احتجوا بقوله ولما ورد ماء مدين يقال لهم: إن موسى لم يمر على تلك البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the saved will not hear Hell’s hiss applies to their time in Paradise; they may have heard it beforehand, or God may make it cool and safe as they enter.
rows.anchor: فكيف يجوز أن يدخلها من قد أخبر الله سبحانه أنه لا يسمع حسيسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They do not enter Hell” can mean they are not kept there forever or are not hurt by it; Qatada glosses being disgraced by the Fire as being eternally kept in it.
rows.anchor: وكذلك تأويل قوله لا يدخلون النار أي لا يخلدون فيها، أو لا يتألمون ويتأذون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues all creatures enter, after which God saves believers—some unharmed and some punished—and eventually admits all of them to Paradise by His mercy.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أن الخلق جميعا يدخلون النار ثم ينجي الله المؤمنين بعضهم سالمين غير آلمين

rows.speaker: حفصة
rows.claim: Hafsa reports the Prophet hoped no one who witnessed Badr and Hudaybiyya would enter Hell; when she cited this verse, he answered by pointing to the promise to save the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: عن أم مبشر عن حفصة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إني أرجو أن لا يدخل النار

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says Hell will rise like a mound of fat; a herald will call it to take its own and leave God’s people, and God’s friends will cross in clean garments.
rows.anchor: عن كعب أنه قال في هذه الآية وإن منكم إلا واردها قال: ترفع جهنم يوم القيامة كأنها متن اهالة

rows.speaker: خالد بن معدان
rows.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan says Paradise’s people ask whether God promised they would arrive at Hell; they are told they passed it while it was extinguished.
rows.anchor: وقال خالد بن معدان: يقول أهل الجنة: ألم يعدنا ربنا أن نرد النار

rows.speaker: يعلى بن منبه
rows.claim: A report from Yaʿla ibn Munya says Hell tells a believer to pass because the believer’s light has extinguished its flame.
rows.anchor: عن يعلى بن منبه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «تقول النار للمؤمن يوم القيامة جز يا مؤمن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says a Muslim’s fever counts as arriving at the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله وإن منكم إلا واردها قال: من حم من المسلمين فقد وردها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The Prophet says people with even a barley seed’s weight of good in their hearts will be brought out of the Fire after professing God’s oneness; those with a grain and an atom’s weight follow.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «يخرج من النار من قال: لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud reads the verb with a different initial vowel, meaning “there.”
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله: ثم ننجي بفتح الثاء يعني هناك

rows.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
rows.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni says: even supposing we are saved, how long will the rescue take?
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا عمران الجوني يقول: هبك ننجو بعد كم ننجو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and other Quraysh; they taunt the Prophet’s poor, rough-clothed, poorly dressed followers while wearing fine clothes and grooming themselves.
rows.anchor: قال الذين كفروا يعني النضر بن الحرث ودونه من قريش للذين آمنوا يعني فقراء أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: أهل مكة
rows.claim: Meccan readers use maqāman with ḍamm, meaning a place or period of residence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل مكة مقاما بالضم أي إقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadiyy means an assembly place, like a club; Dār al-Nadwa was where Quraysh sat and discussed their affairs.
rows.anchor: وأحسن نديا يعني مجلسا، ومثله النادي، ومنه دار الندوة لأن المشركين كانوا يجلسون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that earlier generations He destroyed possessed better furnishings and goods.
rows.anchor: مجيبا لهم وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا أي متاعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains athāthan as appearance or bearing; Muqatil calls it clothing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هيئة وقال مقاتل: ثيابا

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubay reads ziyan instead of riʾyan, meaning appearance or attire.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي: وزيا بالزاي وهو الهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lets the astray continue in transgression until they see the promised worldly punishment or Resurrection, then they will know which group has the worse place and weaker army.
rows.anchor: فليدعه في طغيانه ويمهله في كفره حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases believers in faith and certainty; one explanation says He increases guidance through the abrogating revelation after the abrogated one.
rows.anchor: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى أي إيمانا ويقينا يعني المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining righteous deeds bring a better reward and a better final return.
rows.anchor: والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا عاقبة ومرجعا

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbab reports that al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil, who owed him money, demanded that he renounce Muhammad before paying; al-ʿAs claimed he would have wealth and children after death, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كان لي دين على العاص فأتيته أتقاضاه فقال: لا والله حتى تكفر بمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing are those who avoided idolatry; the wrongdoers are unbelievers left in the Fire, gathered kneeling or on their knees.
rows.anchor: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا يعني اتقوا الشرك وهم المؤمنون

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say Khabbab was a metalworker owed delayed wages by al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil; when Khabbab refused to leave Islam, al-ʿAs mocked that he would repay him in Paradise with a greater share.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان خباب بن الأرت قينا وكان يعمل للعاص بن وائل السهمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boast la-utin means “I will surely be given” wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وقال لأوتين لأعطين مالا وولدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes “has he seen the unseen?” to ask whether the man looked into the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes it to ask whether he knows the unseen, including whether he will be in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أعلم علم الغيب حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أم لا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the covenant with the Merciful as professing that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: يعني أم قال: لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the covenant as a good deed already performed.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني عملا صالحا قدمه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the covenant is God’s assurance that He will admit the man to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عهد إليه أنه يدخله الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects the boast; God will record and preserve what the man says about wealth and children.
rows.anchor: كلا رد عليه يعني لم يفعل ذلك سنكتب سنحفظ عليه ما يقول يعني المال والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man will come to God alone in the afterlife without any worldly possessions.
rows.anchor: ويأتينا فردا في الآخرة ليس معه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s idols will disown their worship in the afterlife and become enemies to them; another view interprets the word as helpers.
rows.anchor: واتخذوا يعني مشركي قريش من دون الله آلهة يعني الأصنام ليكونوا لهم عزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the devils power over unbelievers, as in His instruction to Satan to incite whomever he can.
rows.anchor: ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين يعني سلطناهم عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the devils drive unbelievers from obedience into disobedience.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تزعجهم ازعاجا من الطاعة إلى المعصية

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the devils command people to sin.
rows.anchor:
وقال الضحاك:
يأمرهم بالمعاصي أمرا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the devils entice people toward sin.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: تغريهم إغراء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the devils spur people on forcefully.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تشليهم أشلاء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses the verb as stirring or exciting people.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: توهجهم

rows.speaker: المؤرخ
rows.claim: Al-Muʾarrikh glosses the verb as moving people.
rows.anchor: وقال المؤرخ: تحركهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says the devils mislead, incite, and rouse people.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: تغويهم وتهيجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not hurry punishment for them: God is counting their nights, days, months, and years; another view says He counts their breaths.
rows.anchor: فلا تعجل عليهم بالعذاب إنما نعد لهم عدا

rows.speaker: محمد بن السماك
rows.claim: When the caliph al-Maʾmun asked for admonition on this verse, Ibn al-Sammak warned that counted breaths are quickly exhausted and not renewed.
rows.anchor: التفت إلى محمد بن السماك مشيرا عليه بأن يعظه فقال: إذا كانت الأنفاس بالعدد، ولم يكن لها مدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing are monotheists who approach the Merciful in groups as guests; wafd is a plural like other collective nouns.
rows.anchor: يوم نحشر المتقين يعني الموحدين إلى الرحمن وفدا أي جماعات وهو جمع وافد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra is reported to say that the God-fearing will be gathered riding camels.
rows.anchor: عن رجل عن أبي هريرة يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا قال: على الإبل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they ride camels with gold saddles and reins of emerald.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ركبانا يؤتون بنوق عليها رحال الذهب، وأزمتها الزبرجد

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the devils drive unbelievers into sins; the root conveys movement and boiling, as in a report describing a stomach’s rumbling like a cauldron.
rows.anchor: تخرجهم إلى المعاصي، وأصله الحركة والغليان

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAli says they will not walk: their gold-saddled, jewel-mounted camels travel or fly according to their wish.
rows.anchor: ما يحشرون والله على أرجلهم ولكن على نوق رحالها ذهب، ونجائب سرجها يواقيت

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: In a Prophetic report to ʿAli, angels meet believers with white camels and gold gear, provide heavenly garments, and their mounts carry them to Paradise, where angels welcome them.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا علي إذا كان المنصرف من بين يدي الله تلقت الملائكة المؤمنين بنوق بيض

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the God-fearing arrive as a delegation, honored, given gifts and greetings, and permitted to intercede.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع: يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا قال: يفدون إلى ربهم فيكرمون ويعطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals, meaning unbelievers, are driven to Hell thirsty and on foot, their necks parched; ward denotes a group arriving at water.
rows.anchor: ونسوق المجرمين يعني الكافرين إلى جهنم وردا قال المفسرون: عطاشى، مشاة على أرجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant that permits intercession is professing God’s oneness; Ibn Abbas specifies bearing witness, disavowing one’s own power, and hoping only in God.
rows.anchor: لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا يعني لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing takes the exception to mean that intercession is only for the person who made a covenant with God.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معناه إلا لمن اتخذ، نظيره ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the covenant is belief in God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا يعني اعتقد بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the covenant as acting in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: عمل بطاعة الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud transmits a Prophetic prayer for a daily covenant: profess God’s oneness and Muhammad’s prophethood, ask for protection from one’s own weakness, and seek God’s mercy; the pledge is sealed beneath the Throne and its people enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: سمعت رسول الله علائم يقول لأصحابه ذات يوم: «أيعجز أحدكم أن يتخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who claim God has a child include Jews, Christians, and people who claim the angels are God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا يعني اليهود والنصارى، ومن زعموا أن الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi pronounce walad with ḍamm and a still lām in four places here and in the cited surahs; other readers use fatḥ, reflecting two dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ولدا بضم الواو وجزم اللام وهي أربعة مواضع هاهنا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet’s line uses walad in the cited pronunciation, illustrating the dialect form.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فليت فلانا كان في بطن أمه … وليت فلانا كان ولد حمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat the ḍamm form as plural and the fatḥ form as singular.
rows.anchor: وقيس بجعل الولد بالضم جمعا والولد بالفتح واحدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses iddan as something reprehensible.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: منكرا

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatada and Mujahid gloss iddan as something immense.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد: عظيما

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses it as something atrocious.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فظيعا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it means that they have uttered a tremendous statement, as in the verse calling their claim grave.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: معناه لقد قلتم قولا عظيما، نظيره قوله

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba’s line is cited as poetic evidence for idd meaning a great calamity.
rows.anchor: قال رؤبة: نطح شى أد رؤوس الأداد

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and al-Kisaʾi read the verb preceding “the heavens” in masculine form because the verb comes before its subject.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع والكسائي بالياء لتقديم الفعل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads yanfaṭirna with nun from the verb infaṭara; the author prefers it because it matches other verses about the sky splitting.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ينفطرن بالنون من الانفطار وهو اختيار أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb are associated with a reading meaning “because they attributed a child to the Merciful.”
rows.anchor: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا يعني لأن دعوا، ومن قرأ جعلوا وقالوا للرحمن ولدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the heavens, earth, mountains, and all creatures were alarmed and nearly collapsed when people attributed a child to God; the angels became angry and Hell blazed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب: فزعت السموات والأرض والجبال وجميع الخلائق إلا الثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not described as taking a child: He neither does so nor needs to, and the description does not apply to Him.
rows.anchor: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا يعني انه لا يفعل ذلك ولا يحتاج إليه ولا يوصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every being in heaven and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant, not a child; God counts their breaths and days, and each will come alone without worldly possessions.
rows.anchor: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا لا ولدا لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, idd denotes the greatest calamities; the term has three dialect forms, with kasra the common reading.
rows.anchor: إد بالكسر وهي قراءة العامة
